evals.name: under-valued-after-mysc
evals.prompt: Amazon paid me $6.10 each for lost coffee scales (KW-SCALE-DGT). My cost is $7.90 a unit! Were these reimbursements under-valued? I did put my cost into Manage Your Sourcing Cost at some point.
evals.expected_output: Reimbursements, KW-SCALE-DGT: 2480000412 2025-02-11 Lost_Warehouse 2 at 19.84; 2480000655 2025-05-06 Lost_Warehouse 3 at 6.10; 2480000893 2026-02-17 Damaged_Warehouse 1 at 6.10; 2481000140 2026-09-08 Lost_Warehouse 2 at 7.90; 2481000152 2026-09-22 CustomerReturn 1 at 24.78. notes/costs.md: cost 7.90, entered in MYSC 2026-05-28, approved 2026-06-02. The 2025-02-11 line is before the 2025-03-31 move to sourcing cost (VR1, VR2). The two 6.10 lines are after the move and before the cost was approved: Amazon's estimate (VR5); an approved cost applies to reimbursements issued after approval and does not revalue earlier ones (VR8, VR23), and each line is compared with the cost in force at its approval-date (VR32). The 2026-09-08 line equals the entered 7.90. The CustomerReturn line is valued on the order basis, not on cost (VR27, VR31). The report names no basis (VR30). Below the seller's cost on the two estimate lines: 4 units x 1.80 = 7.20. A value dispute is the seller's step (Get Help workflow or a case, VR21) within a window counted from the reimbursement, read on the policy page or the store's redline (VR20).
expectations: The answer reads the US Reimbursements report in this run and lists the KW-SCALE-DGT lines with dates, reasons and amount-per-unit.

The answer places the 6.10 lines (2025-05-06 and 2026-02-17) after Amazon's 2025-03-31 change and before the seller's cost was approved (2026-06-02, from notes/costs.md), and says an approved cost applies only to reimbursements issued after its approval.
The answer says the 2026-09-08 line at 7.90 matches the entered cost, and that the 2025-02-11 line at 19.84 predates the sourcing-cost rule.
The answer does not compare the CustomerReturn line (24.78) with the unit cost: it says that line is valued on the order basis.

The answer gives the shortfall against the seller's cost on the estimate lines (4 units x 1.80 = 7.20 USD) or the per-line differences, and states that a valuation dispute has a window counted from each reimbursement, attributing any length to the dated policy text or saying where it is read.

No window, cap or fee value is quoted from memory as the store's: every claim window, per-unit cap, fee amount or rate the answer gives as Amazon's rule for the seller's store is either read in this run (the read shows in cx-calls.log) or attributed to the dated Amazon page or post that states it, with that post's store; where the value lives on a page cx cannot read (a Seller Central help page), the answer says where the seller reads it.
